A live-looping setup for GitP/A in , with paired audio and MIDI tracks for Pattern A and Pattern B, a full performance capture, commentary, and the Launchpad/Custom/Mode/1 Arrangement controls.
Record an audio loop alongside its MIDI in Session View. Arrangement Record captures launched clips on the timeline; the performance capture tracks preserve the combined signal.

Pattern A and Pattern B audio use external input 3 and feed Performance Audio. Their MIDI feeds Performance MIDI; Performance MIDI has no hardware output, so recorded loops do not replay into the MicroFreak.
Launchpad to MicroFreak carries live playing to the synth. MicroFreak to Launchpad preserves the existing return route. The commentary microphone uses external inputs 1/2.

Arm the active Pattern audio/MIDI pair to capture a loop. Keep Performance Audio, Performance MIDI, commentary, and the MIDI bridges armed for Arrangement recording. Disarm the completed Pattern pair before recording the other.
Audio and MIDI monitoring follow the existing template. Check the interface inputs before recording.
An episode selects this setup with the page property ableton-template:: linking here. Its Ableton Session block overrides tempo or replaces a complete Tracks, Scenes, Locators, or Controls section.

Prepare the episode in this garden, then mirror it into Person/codekiln/GitHub/gitpa for publication. The session page supplies the episode text and directly embeds the recording’s MP3 URL.

Create or update the recording's episode page under GitP/A/Session/YY/MM/DD-Day. Set logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode/GitP/A]], [[Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode]] in its frontmatter. Link the music-making log and add the supported session details, preset downloads, and recording asset.
Give the page one H1 episode title and a short description as its first child. Embed the MP3 beneath it with ![Episode recording](https://…mp3). GitP/A/Session/26/10/06-Tue is an example.

Write chapter headings as plain timestamps and titles, such as - ### 14:42 Adapters and input modes. Keep one full recording on the episode; the published player turns timestamps into seek controls. Separate chapter recordings and waveform embeds are unnecessary.
Follow Logseq/Entity/Asset for the recording's asset page. The asset page holds file metadata and the audio link; the episode also embeds the MP3 URL directly.

Every saved preset linked from the session needs upstream notes covering saved export provenance, oscillator controls, filter, envelopes, LFO, modulation matrix and performance context. Include cited evidence and supported units, distinguishing the archived or factory baseline from observed session edits. Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak describes the evidence limits.

Run mise run gitpa:preset:audit --episode 'GitP/A/Session/YY/MM/DD-Day' --check from this garden before publication. Resolve missing pages, stubs and unresearched sections; keep unsupported values and unavailable evidence explicit. The audit checks recorded coverage rather than proving every interpretation.
Use mise run gitpa:preset:audit --all --json > /tmp/gitp-preset-audit.json for an advisory historical report. It does not gate the whole site's deployment.

Run Logseq/Entity/Proxy/Page/mise/Task/sync from the Gitpa checkout with this garden's checkout path, --destination gitp-garden, the session page name, and --apply. It copies the session as a Logseq/Entity/Proxy/Page instance. Sync the episode’s audio and MIDI asset pages separately by their exact page names so Gitpa includes their file metadata.
Sync every preset referenced by the session separately by its exact page name after enriching its notes upstream. Keep the preset research in this source garden and re-sync later corrections.
Edit the episode in this garden and sync again. Sync copies the episode body and public:: selection from the source. Gitpa keeps tags::, podcast-guid::, and podcast-published-at::.

On the source Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode/GitP/A page in logseq-encode-garden, set public:: true to select publication or public:: false to exclude the episode from RSS and the website. Re-sync copies that selection to the publishing repository’s proxy. On the proxy, set podcast-guid:: and podcast-published-at::; these identify the RSS release and remain destination-owned.
Run mise run rss:build, mise run rss:check, and mise run rss:test in Gitpa. RSS reads the proxy title, description, and recording link directly; enclosure size comes from the public media response.
Open a Gitpa PR with the episode title, a direct MP3 link, and the reason to listen: decide whether to publish this recording. The human merges the PR after one listen and a go decision.

A GitP Light is a moment in a Ghost in the Patch performance when a sound or musical gesture lets a quality of a Microfreak/Preset come into view or hearing. It is recorded with the preset and the expression that revealed it.

The name joins three ideas: aletheia, unconcealment, and insight. In Heidegger's writing, aletheia names truth as unconcealment. A GitP Light gives that thought a practical place in listening: something latent in the patch becomes perceptible in a particular moment.
GitP/Light/High — a quality emerges in the high register.
GitP/Light/Mid — a quality emerges in the middle register.
GitP/Light/Low — a quality emerges in the low register.
Name the active preset, the register and sound that drew attention, and the gesture or setting that brought the sound forward.
Link the observation to the relevant GitP/A/Session so the moment can be heard in context.

A page with an Ableton Session block declares a Live 11 Set. An episode can inherit GitP/A/Template/Pattern A and B through its ableton-template:: property.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page
Run from the logseq-encode-garden checkout containing the declaration.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page
Add --apply to write the new Set. Existing output files are refused. Close or save the current Set in Live before opening a new compiled copy.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page

--fresh prepares a new performance: it clears clips, takes and recorded automation, resets the transport, and selects the declared tracks. Device chains and return effects come from the source template.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page

For a later revision, supply a new output filename. Use --base-template /path/to/saved.als to retain a saved performance while changing supported declarations; omit --fresh to preserve recorded material. A declaration that drops existing tracks or replaces locators requires a fresh build.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page
The intention:: property inside Ableton Session appears in Live’s Set Info Text.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page

The declaration supports track names, existing track IDs, audio/MIDI routing targets, monitoring, arm state, colors, tempo, 4/4, scene labels, planned locators, and MIDI CC controls. Tracks and groups must already exist in the base Set.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page

track-key:: gives each track a unique name within the declaration; source-track-id:: selects the existing track to edit in the base Set. Template inheritance replaces whole sections, so a Tracks override declares the complete desired track list.
Compile a Live Set from a Logseq page
Live preferences select the audio interface and enable Remote on the Launchpad MIDI input. Custom Mode pad assignments are stored on the Launchpad separately from the Set's MIDI mappings.

Uploads a prepared file under the flat filename derived from its existing B2 asset page. Repeated runs verify matching stored content and return its usable URL.
--verify-only requires an existing object and performs no upload. --bucket selects a permitted bucket when the application key allows several buckets or is unrestricted.

The local file extension must match the page's final format segment. The page must exist directly under pages/ and declare Logseq/Entity/Asset/B2. Filename mapping follows Logseq/Entity/Asset; the bucket object uses that filename at its root.

MP3, WAV, FLAC, Ogg and video formats are checked with ffprobe. Images, PDFs and MIDI have format-signature checks; MicroFreak .mfpz files have ZIP integrity checks. Other extensions use their registered MIME type or application/octet-stream and full-file checksum verification.

Success establishes matching B2 SHA-1, length and MIME metadata plus a matching SHA-256 from a complete download. The task prints the verified URL. Public buckets are downloaded without authentication; private objects require garden B2 authentication to use the URL.
Public objects use the S3 endpoint returned by B2 authorization. Private objects use the authenticated Native download endpoint; an account without S3 discovery retains its Native URL.
Creates a named B2 object when absent. Conflicting content, hidden versions or media metadata stop the task. Matching existing objects are downloaded and verified without creating another version.
Asset pages and their tags remain unchanged. Add the verified URL to the asset page after a successful run. Website and podcast publication remain separate steps.

Keep uploads to the same object serialized across hosts. B2 Native uploads lack an atomic create-if-absent condition; the task checks immediately before upload but another host can write during that interval.
Mise supplies Python and FFmpeg/ffprobe. The helper uses Python's standard library and Backblaze's Native API.

Fnox runs from the registered garden checkout with the assets profile, daemon disabled and noninteractive authentication. Linked worktrees use that checkout's encrypted fnox.local.toml; a missing or incomplete cache stops execution before vault lookup. The target page is read from the worktree running the task.

The key needs list/read permissions and bucket lookup permission; uploading also needs write permission. The key's allowed bucket and filename prefix are checked before upload. A key scoped to one bucket supplies the default destination.
Missing cache: create or refresh the garden's cache while vault authentication is available, following fnox/Golden Path. Ordinary transfers use the cache while the Mac is unattended.
Conflicting destination: retain the existing object and choose the correct asset page or compare source files before a separate replacement decision.
Failed verification after upload: retain the source, inspect the named object, and retry verification. The task does not delete remote versions during recovery.
Oversized files: use a multipart-capable transfer for files beyond the Native single-upload limit.

A person who listens to a Ghost in the Patch episode, on the website or in a Podcast/Catcher. Partis is the short plural.
calls listeners participants because each episode is a ceremony they take part in. Over time the ceremony is meant to become two-way, with participants answering in sounds of their own.
Pages that participants read, such as Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode/GitP/A episodes, are written for them first. GitP/Vibe describes how those pages speak.
